messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Stan crashed R
parts:
The other day I told Bob that Stan often crashed R. He told me that this was not good and I should let him know when this next happens. I responded that it happens a lot but seems to be something that occurs because of various things happening in the R session, with the Stan call being the straw that breaks the camel’s back.

Anyway, Stan crashed R today. But when I reopened it the model ran fine. This is behavior that is hard for me to reproduce because it seems to be a consequence of various wrong models trying to run and filling up the R space with bad stuff. Who knows?

I could share the code but there hardly seems any point to this given that it runs fine now. Anyway, I just wanted to let you know that this is still happening.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Stan crashed R
parts:
If you are loading objects that were created by a previous version of rstan, then I wouldn't trust them to work correctly. I think it has been months since anyone else reported crashing R with rstan.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Stan crashed R
parts:
Can you send us model, data, and random seeds?
If so, we should be able to reproduce your behavior.
That is, if you give us all your version information:

OS version, Xcode version, R version, Rcpp version,
Stan version, RStudio version (if you're running that).

I'm particularly concerned that we don't have bugs in Stan
where things might segfault and crash any process they're
running in.

And you're running in RStudio, right? With or without parallelization?
(You really have to figure out how to parallelize if you're
running Stan for anything other than toy problems.)

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan crashed R
parts:
Hi, I don’t have the random seeds (can’t recover them either, since R crashed). But I’m pretty sure that even with the same random seeds, the model would not crash R on its own.

But if I can ever get Stan to crash R on a regular basis, I’ll definitely give you all the information!

Also, I don’t think the problem is with Rstudio, because when Stan crashes Rstudio, it also does similar things in the plain R console.

Finally, I don’t know if I’m using parallelization. I’ve been using Sebastian’s stan_run() function. I can try switching to Ben’s new function that he wrote that does paralellization.
